dedupe_keys.name: maris open data graph of critical infrastructure dependencies for central rome

description: This case study builds a graph of critical infrastructure dependencies for a central area of Rome from open data, using the MARIS methodology (Modeling infrAstructuRe dependencIes at an urban Scale). Antonio Di Pietro and colleagues from ENEA, Tesseract, Sapienza University and the University of British Columbia published it as an open access book chapter in November 2023. System-level dependencies from a survey of Italian experts are scaled down to individual assets taken from OpenStreetMap with Taginfo and Overpass turbo, and where operators' data are missing each asset is tied to the nearest supplier, for example a hospital to the closest substation. The resulting graph has 6,025 entities in 10 systems, including 1,000 substations, 122 telecom base stations, 31 hospitals and 188 rail stations. Coverage is one district of Rome. Format and access: a free chapter; the graph itself is not released. Licence: open access chapter, terms not recorded. Caveats: proximity rules stand in for real supply links, and OSM completeness varies. It is a template for building cascading failure and emergency simulation inputs when operator data are confidential. Related catalogue records are the I2Sim interdependency simulator and the German inter 3 KRITIS interdependency guide.
